question: Does the pinned Artemis II transcript contain enough new, target-localized, observer-diverse, morphology-controlled directional roughness claims to admit a controlled multi-target LOLA continuation without inventing regions or reusing exposed outcomes?
terminal_objective: Decide whether Stage 7A can advance to a controlled same-endpoint panel before any new instrument-value access.
baseline: Stop after transcript-only admission review. One strong Stage 7A pair does not justify constructing additional regions after seeing source values.
treatment: Inventory every plausible texture-language episode, apply frozen localization, endpoint, independence, observer, morphology, and control gates, and permit new LOLA access only if the complete panel passes.
shared_endpoint: LOLA median absolute slope over prospectively fixed equal-physical-area regions
claim_ceiling: A verified stop establishes only that the pinned transcript cannot support the predeclared controlled same-endpoint multi-target continuation without reuse, post hoc localization, endpoint mixing, or missing controls. It does not refute Stage 7A, the broader value of astronaut language, the two cross-axis candidates, or the possibility that new independently coded observations could form a valid panel.

next_step_logic.if_admitted: Freeze all target and control geometries, source revisions, and thresholds before any additional instrument-value access, then run offline from hash-pinned bounded products.
next_step_logic.if_stopped: Do not access more LOLA values for this lane. Treat Reiner Gamma albedo uniformity and Glushko-versus-Ohm ray brightness only as candidates for a separately preregistered cross-axis panel with endpoint-specific controls.
next_step_logic.if_indeterminate: Repair only a named transcript identity or coding-boundary defect; do not weaken the admission thresholds.
